newsitem.title: USA: S&P rates Akron, Ohio, bonds AA-minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Akron, Ohio, bonds AA-minus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's today has assigned its double-A'-minus rating to Akron, Ohio's $3.8 million various purpose improvement bonds series 1996 and $2.51 million street improvement bonds series 1996.
The double-A'-minus rating on the city's $80.69 million G.O. parity debt has been affirmed. The rating reflects:
-- Steadily decreasing dependence on tire manufacturing,
-- Strong financial operations marked by a diverse revenue stream, and

Akron's economy has successfully diversified away from a heavy dependence on tire manufacturing by expanding its trade and service sectors. Employment in health and financial services has expanded, and the city's downtown efforts have produced further growth in trade and service jobs. The city hopes to spur further downtown development with the National Investors Hall of Fame and Science Museum and the planned opening of a minor league baseball stadium in 1997. The city continues to attract polymer-related industries, including Advanced Elastomer Systems in 1995, with an initial employment of 195. Although higher than the state's average of 4.8%, the city's unemployment rate is down significantly from the double-digit rates of the mid-1980s, averaging 6.4% in 1994.

Financial performance remains sound, based on revenue diversity, expense controls, conservative budget practices, and a sound fund balance policy. Local income tax revenues represented 50% of revenues, while property taxes contributed 11% and licenses, fees, and charges contributed 20%. The unreserved general fund balance remained strong in 1995 at $13.4 million, or 12% of expenditures, despite a drawdown for unusually large snow removal expenses. Revenues and expenditures are currently on pace with the budget in 1996. The city has significant flexibility under the 10.5 mill property tax limit, with 20% remaining. The city also levies a 2% income tax, with 27% of the revenues earmarked for capital improvements and debt service, and the remainder supporting operations, specifically the city's police and fire departments.

The debt burden is manageable at $779 per capita and 2.5% of market value. Future debt includes approximately $20 million in limited tax general obligation debt this fall and approximately $30 million in certificates of participation to finance the minor league stadium within the next month. Approximately $3 million of the various purpose bond proceeds will be used to finance a settlement with the Ohio Water Development Authority, and $800,000 for costs associated with the Inventor's Hall of Fame. The proceeds of the street improvements bonds are for various improvements in the city.
The outlook is based on a diversifying economic base, taxing flexibility, and strong financial operations, Standard & Poor's said.
